definition.heading: What are learning and development solutions?
definition.lede: The short answer, and why it beats buying training one course at a time.
definition.answer: Learning and development (L&D) solutions are the services and tools a company uses to build its people's skills and prove the change. They cover three layers: diagnosing what the business needs, building skills through training, coaching and leadership programs, and delivering and running it all at scale.
definition.more: Large companies staff each layer with their own learning and development team. Growing companies rarely can. Edstellar covers all three as one partner, so you get the strategy, the programs and the delivery without hiring an L&D department or managing several vendors.

items.question: What are learning and development solutions?
items.answer: Learning and development (L&D) solutions are the services and tools a company uses to build its people's skills and prove the change. They usually cover three layers: strategy and consulting, learning and talent programs such as training, coaching and leadership development, and the delivery, platforms and reporting that run it all.

items.question: What do Edstellar's L&D solutions include?
items.answer: Training needs analysis, talent assessments, L&D consulting, OD consulting, corporate training, leadership development, coaching, team effectiveness, managed learning services, and Edstellar's own platforms, including Spectra LMS and Capability OS. Each one can run on its own or as part of a complete L&D plan.

items.question: Do you work with small and mid-sized companies?
items.answer: Yes. Edstellar's L&D solutions are designed for growing companies, from start-ups to mid-sized businesses, and also serve global enterprises. Engagements are modular, so a smaller company can start with one program for one team and add more as it grows.

items.question: Do we need an in-house L&D team to work with Edstellar?
items.answer: No. Many clients have one HR lead, or no L&D role at all. Edstellar can plan, run and report on learning for you through managed learning services, or support the team you already have.

items.question: Can Edstellar deliver training across multiple countries and languages?
items.answer: Yes. Edstellar delivers the same program across locations in 100+ countries, onsite, virtually or blended, in 10+ languages including English, Spanish, Mandarin, Portuguese, Arabic and German. You work with one partner and get one consolidated report across every country.

items.question: Can Edstellar run our L&D for us?
items.answer: Yes. Edstellar can run part or all of your L&D, from advisory support to an end-to-end managed function. See learning and development outsourcing for the engagement models and how the transition works.

items.question: How is an L&D solution different from corporate training?
items.answer: Corporate training is one part of learning and development. A complete L&D solution starts from the skills the business needs, measures them before and after, and combines training with coaching, assessments, consulting and on-the-job support. For training programs on their own, see Edstellar corporate training.

items.question: How much do learning and development solutions cost?
items.answer: Cost depends on scope: the number of people, programs, formats and locations. Because engagements are modular, you can start with one program at a fixed scope rather than a large contract. After a 30-minute briefing, Edstellar sends a scoped proposal within one business day.

items.question: How do you measure the impact of L&D programs?
items.answer: Edstellar measures skills by role, using validated assessments, 360-degree feedback, manager ratings and work evidence. Each skill is rated on clear proficiency levels, and every engagement is tied to a business metric, so progress shows up as real change, not course completions.

items.question: How long does it take to get started?
items.answer: A single training or coaching program can start soon after scoping. A full L&D plan usually takes three to five months for its first cycle: about 6 to 10 weeks to assess, analyze and design, then 6 to 12 weeks of delivery.
